author: LeadershipNGA
title: Federal Government Begins National Control Centre Construction in Osogbo
text:
The federal government has begun construction of an ultra-modern National Control Centre in Osogbo, Osun State, to replace a 64-year-old facility and stabilise Nigeria's grid.
The federal government has begun construction of an ultra-modern National Control Centre in Osogbo, Osun State, ending what officials described as a 64-year-old jinx. The groundbreaking was held on Wednesday on behalf of Vice President Kashim Shettima, who was represented by Bashir Maidugu, Senior Special Assistant (Legal) in the Office of the Vice President. The Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, joined the delegation at the site.
The facility is designed for the Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO) and will replace an obsolete installation that is six decades old. According to the government, the existing equipment can no longer cope with the operational pressures of Nigeria's evolving electricity grid.
New Control Centre to Modernise National Grid
Tegbe said the upcoming facility will give NISO complete, real-time visibility across the entire national grid network, enabling rapid intervention during system swings. He described the initiative as tangible proof of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu's resolve to address systemic vulnerabilities across the electricity value chain.
Upon completion and commissioning, the complex will feature fully integrated Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition systems, high-definition large-format display walls, and advanced grid analytics. These tools will allow system operators to identify emerging electrical faults before they escalate, schedule targeted preventive maintenance, and maximise the throughput of available generation and transmission assets.
The centre is also engineered to strengthen disturbance management, ease the integration of utility-scale renewable energy resources, and reinforce Nigeria's leadership and synchronisation within the West African Power Pool. The facility will be protected by advanced physical and cybersecurity architectures.
Reliability Gains for Households and Businesses
Addressing the expected benefits for households and commercial enterprises, Tegbe said the primary outcome will be a sharp decline in preventable blackouts and a noticeably more stable supply. He stressed that grid reliability is a holistic effort requiring sustained gas feedstock delivery, robust maintenance of high-voltage transmission lines, and capable distribution infrastructure to evacuate power to end consumers.
The new control hub, he added, will provide the precise operational coordination needed to translate upstream investments into stable, delivered electricity. Maidugu underscored that a stable and resilient power sector sits at the heart of President Tinubu's Renewed Hope Agenda.
He noted that sustainable electricity forms the bedrock of an effective economy, one that empowers industrial manufacturers to schedule production lines seamlessly, allows small business owners to run their ventures predictably, ensures critical public services such as hospitals and schools stay functional, and unlocks employment alongside broad economic opportunities.
Maidugu emphasised that the National Control Centre serves as the nerve centre safeguarding operational reliability, warning that Nigeria cannot manage a modern, dynamic and interconnected transmission network using outdated legacy equipment.
NISO Highlights Data and Workforce Readiness
Also speaking at the event, Abdu Bello Mohammed, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of NISO, affirmed that the facility will dramatically elevate the operator's surveillance, streamline day-to-day coordination, and drive fast, evidence-based mitigation whenever disturbances hit the network, thereby solidifying energy security.
He stated that enriched data pipelines powered by advanced telemetry, next-generation SCADA, and automatic meter reading will drive superior operational choices, deliver higher supply reliability, and bring precision to wholesale market settlements.
Mohammed added that the facility will position NISO to meet the rigorous technical codes of the regional West African electricity grid. He noted in parallel that NISO is actively training elite personnel to manage the infrastructure to global benchmarks, acknowledging that modern technology depends on capable human operators to succeed.
The milestone event drew an extensive delegation of dignitaries, including the Board and Executive Management of NISO, members of the Senate and House Committees on Power, chief executives of electricity Distribution Companies, delegates of the Osun State Government, power sector investors, and host community leaders.
